text:
sophie: quick follow-up to the safetensors warmup thread — I sketched an idea: instead of shipping full replacement checkpoints for 1-2MB fixes (tokenizer tweaks, small quant corrections, layer-wise fixes), we could publish delta patches per-shard and apply them on-demand during warmup. goal: reduce storage + network churn and avoid rehydrating whole checkpoint for small fixes. thoughts? :thinking_face:

Derek: sounds interesting. two immediate Qs: how do we verify integrity (signed diffs?) and what does the loader contract look like when overlaying a delta on top of a shard already streamed to disk?

sophie: yep — proposal: base shard stays content-addressed (cid/base). we publish small patch objects (cid/patch) plus a signed patch-manifest that lists target shard cid, patch cid, patch type (binary-delta | overlay | rename), and a HMAC signature. loader behavior: if request arrives and patch exists, apply patch in-memory before KV-cache allocation, fallback to full shard if patch apply fails.

maria: CPU/latency concern: applying binary deltas at runtime for the first request could add 30-200ms per shard depending on size. for models with many shards that kills cold-starts. can we precompute a "hot" merged artifact on the edge for high-QPS customers? or offload apply to a small patcher service that writes merged shards to local disk asynchronously?

jon: +1 to offload. alternative: lazy-apply but with priority hints. idea: manifest includes patch.priority = {0..3}; loader applies priority=3 synchronously, enqueues priority 1-2 to background patcher that will write merged blob to local cache. then future requests use the merged path.

sophie: good call. here's a minimal manifest snippet I had in mind:
```
{
  "base_shard": "sha256:abc...",
  "patches": [
    { "patch_cid": "sha256:def...", "type": "xdelta", "priority": 3, "size": 12345 }
  ]
}
```
loader semantics: try apply in-memory when priority >= sync_threshold, otherwise background.

tariq: another gotcha: GPU memory residency. if loader applies patch in CPU land and then copies to GPU, any mismatch in memory layout (alignment/padding from delta) could trip fastpath assumptions in runtime. we need a small verification step post-apply that computes a cheap checksum over the regions we care about (e.g., weight tensors used by fused-kernels) and rejects apply if layout deviates beyond allowed patterns.

maria: +1. also add a metric: patch_apply_latency and patch_apply_failures. we should gate background patch writes by IO budget so we don't thrash SSDs during heavy builds.

jon: compatibility with existing safetensors loader: keep base format unchanged. treat patches as a higher-layer overlay — loader checks for manifest sidecar (same key + .patch.json). if none, behave as today. that keeps rollout simple.

Derek: about signature verification: manifest should be signed with the same signing key we use for model releases. patch objects optional signed. if manifest signature fails, reject patch. also we should record provenance (who published patch) and TTL for auto-revert.

sophie: thinking about rollback — patches should be transactional across shards for a given release id. manifest should include transaction_id and we need a cheap two-phase commit: publish manifest.pending -> once distributed, flip manifest.active. loader honors active only. that avoids partial patch states on some nodes.

tariq: ops note: implement a fast-path fallback — if patch apply times out > 500ms, fallback to streaming base shard + use compatibility kernel that tolerates small layout diffs. this prevents user-facing latency spikes.

maria: storage savings calc: for a 80GB model with 80 shards, a tiny per-shard 1MB delta across 10% of shards is ~8MB vs full 80GB reupload — huge win. but we need a cleanup policy: patches older than X with no traffic should be GC'd. add patch.reference_count and last_access_ts to manifest for GC heuristics.

jon: testing: add unit for patch-apply deterministic output + fuzz test for corrupted patches. prod integration: roll out on canary nodes with slow traffic first.

build-bot: integration-tests / patcher-service compiled and passed on canary. 3 tests failed (xdelta-corrupt), filing flaky test ticket #4628 :white_check_mark:

sophie: nice. next steps: I'll write a short RFC with manifest shape, loader finite-state-machine, patcher-service API, and metrics. @derek @maria can you be reviewers?

Derek: happy to.

maria: I'll review, want to add IO budget details + GC policy.

jon: ping me if you want a prototype for the background writer (I have something small).

sophie: thanks all — I'll post the RFC in #eng-ml and link back here. :rocket:
